title: Sam Xu
text:
I graduated from the University of Toronto and spent the past three and a half years working in property and casualty (P&C) insurance, where I developed experience working with data and quantitative actuarial models. That experience made me increasingly interested in what lies beyond traditional analytical methods, particularly the ways machine learning and AI can expand how complex problems are modelled and solved.
I am currently pursuing the Master of Data Science at UBC to deepen my skills in machine learning, AI, agentic programming, and modern data workflows. I am particularly interested in building and validating automated modelling pipelines, integrating AI effectively into analytical workflows, and developing stronger software-engineering practices through my data science training.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
My first week in the MDS program was mainly about getting oriented to the program, the schedule, and the tools we will be using throughout the year. There was a lot of information to absorb, but it was useful to see how the different courses and platforms fit together.
One thing that stood out to me was how intensive and structured the program is. Even in the first week, we were already working with tools such as Git, GitHub, Quarto, Python, and R, so it quickly became clear that the program would involve both technical learning and learning how to work efficiently.
After the first few days, I started to feel more comfortable with the workflow and expectations. I am still adjusting to the pace, but I am looking forward to developing stronger programming and data science skills over the coming months.

title: About Me
text:
Why Data Science
Working with data and loss models made me increasingly interested in methods beyond the traditional actuarial approaches I had been using. In particular, I became interested in machine learning, AI, and how stronger programming and automation can improve analytical actuarial works. I joined UBC’s Master of Data Science program to develop these capabilities more systematically, from statistical and machine-learning methods to programming, data workflows, and collaborative software development.

title: About Me
text:
What I Want to Build
I am particularly interested in moving beyond simply using AI tools toward building reliable AI-enabled analytical workflows. I want to strengthen my ability to develop and validate modelling pipelines, automate repetitive analytical processes, and apply stronger software-engineering practices through my data science training. Over time, I hope to combine these skills with my industry experience to build tools and models that are technically sound and useful in practice.
